objective: Retain the dense-data baseline's observed persistent structural recovery with less training compute through improved sampling.
validation: 66 tests passed in 10.23 seconds before batch 1.
batch_1: Paired dense rerun and 16384-point balanced cycling through the same saved dense pools. Frozen hypothesis, controls, guardrails and branching criteria in batch-1.json.
fresh_cases: Reserved and not evaluated; SHA-256 checked before and after each batch.
batch_1_result: Audited: 16384 cycling qualifies, 6/6 persistent, 75% fewer presentations and 61.4% less measured training time than concurrent dense rerun; all 18 dense model/Adam checkpoints reproduce exactly.
batch_2_result: Audited negative: 4096 cycling has 5/6 persistent passes and exceeds independent gap RMSE tolerance at both later checkpoints, despite all six final structural passes.
batch_3: Preregistered 8192-point cycling, selected according to the batch-2 decision branch. Final batch regardless of result.
batch_3_result: Audited negative: 8192 cycling meets error guardrails but has only 5/6 persistent structural passes. All six final checkpoints pass; local seed 33 fails at 26000.
next_action: Goal completed. No further training or evaluation in this campaign. Proposed next study: preregister block-order robustness for 16384 cycling on development geometry before consuming reserved fresh cases.
